title: When was the last time…?

Stage 1 · Intro

Stage 5 · Grammar

Grammar

The Past Simple — regular verbs.
In other words
“Last night I cooked spaghetti.”
“I called a taxi yesterday.”
“She lived in Vietnam ten years ago.”
“We studied all night at university.”
Notice

Notice: look at the end of each verb. What do we add to make the past?

Verb ends in…RuleExample
most verbs+ edwork → worked · help → helped
-e+ dlive → lived · move → moved
consonant + yy → iedstudy → studied · carry → carried
one vowel + one consonantdouble + edstop → stopped · chat → chatted
In other words
Use the Past Simple for finished actions with a finished time: yesterday, last week, two days ago.
Regular verbs add -ed. The form is the same for ALL persons: I cooked, she cooked, they cooked.
Watch the spelling: live → lived, study → studied, stop → stopped.
Irregular verbs (go → went, have → had) come in Lesson 3.

Stage 6 · Sounds

Sounds

-ed has three sounds. Listen.

helped ends in /t/ · listened ends in /d/ · waited ends in /ɪd/ — an extra syllable.

Track 6.5 — the three -ed soundsOriginal coursebook recording
Track 6.7 — fourteen verbs, sortedOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
/d/ — opened, returned, called, copied, believed, loved, moved, prepared, received, used. /t/ — finished, looked, thanked, liked, noticed, worked. /ɪd/ — started, collected, visited, posted, shouted, waited, wanted.
1helped — which sound?
2listened — which sound?
3waited — which sound?
4worked — which sound?
5loved — which sound?
6wanted — which sound?
Why

/t/ after quiet sounds (helped, worked) · /d/ after noisy sounds (listened, loved) · /ɪd/ after t and d (waited, wanted).

23 — change…

Why

You heard: cooked · change · wait · chatted. The -ed ending tells you it is past.

1finished — which sound?
2moved — which sound?
3visited — which sound?
4liked — which sound?
Why

/t/ after quiet sounds (finished, liked) · /d/ after noisy sounds (moved) · /ɪd/ after t and d (visited).

1 My friends cooked a great meal for me last night. 2 A lot of people at work listen to the radio these days. 3 I helped my parents a lot when I was a child. 4 We dance a lot when we go out. 5 I waited a long time for the bus last Monday. 6 I washed the car carefully, it was really dirty.
11 — My friends ___ a great meal.
22 — People at work ___ to the radio.
34 — We ___ a lot when we go out.
45 — I ___ a long time for the bus.
Why

cooked last night (past) · listen these days (present) · dance when we go out (present) · waited last Monday (past). The time words help you too.

3visited — which sound?
4liked — which sound?
Why

Stage 7 · Practice

Practice

Part 1 — Make the past form. Choose the correct spelling.
1Yesterday I ___ English. (study)
2We ___ at a small hotel. (stay)
3She ___ in Vietnam ten years ago. (live)
4The bus ___ at the station. (stop)
5They ___ football at the weekend. (play)
6He ___ in Astana last Monday. (arrive)
Why

studied (y→ied) · stayed (vowel+y just +ed) · lived · stopped (double) · played · arrived.

1❌ “I visitted my aunt last week.”
2❌ “He arriveed late.”
3❌ “We was watched TV last night.”
4❌ “She carryed the bags home.”
Why

visited (no double t) · arrived · we watched (no was!) · carried.

1The party ___ fun. We danced all night.
2We ___ very tired after the party.
3I ___ a film last night.
4My parents ___ at home yesterday.
Why

be → was/were (the party was, we were). Action verbs → -ed (watched, danced).

1He ___ work at six. (finish)
2We ___ to Turkey last summer. (travel)
3She ___ the bags home. (carry)
4The film ___ at nine. (start)
Why

finished · travelled · carried · started.

1❌ “They stayd at a hotel.”
2❌ “I studyed English last night.”
3❌ “She was cooked dinner yesterday.”
Why

stayed · studied · she cooked (no was before an action verb!).

1The concert ___ great. We listened for two hours.
2We ___ happy after the concert.
3They ___ in a small hotel last week.
Why

be → was/were. Action verbs → -ed: stayed (never “were stayed”).

Stage 8 · Listen

Listen

Track 6.9 — when was the last time…?Original coursebook recording
Show transcript
1 — moved house? — In 2010. From an apartment to a house. 2 — received an email? — This morning. It was from my boss. 3 — prepared a meal? — Last night. I cooked spaghetti for my housemate. 4 — posted a letter? — A month ago. It was to my friend in Australia. 5 — shouted at someone? — About a week ago. My son was very naughty. 6 — visited a relative? — Last summer. I travelled to Kenya to see my grandmother. 7 — called a taxi? — Yesterday. I was late for work. 8 — entered a competition? — When I was a child. I was in a swimming race. 9 — used a dictionary? — Last week. I checked the meaning of 'coin'. 10 — waited for a long time? — Two hours ago. My bus was very late.
People answer: “When was the last time you…?”

Listen. Then choose the answer you heard.

1When was the last time she moved house?
2When did he prepare a meal?
3Why did she call a taxi yesterday?
4Who did he visit in Kenya last summer?
5How long ago did she wait for the bus?
Why

Moved house — in 2010 · cooked spaghetti last night · called a taxi because she was late for work · visited his grandmother in Kenya · waited two hours ago.

People answer: “When was the last time you…?”

Listen. Then choose True or False.

1She moved house in 2010.
2He cooked spaghetti this morning.
3She posted a letter to a friend in Australia.
4He visited his grandfather in Kenya.
Why

He cooked spaghetti last night, not this morning. In Kenya he visited his grandmother.

Stage 9 · Write

Write

Write five true sentences about the last time you did things.

Use -ed verbs and a time expression in every sentence.

Useful language
  • The last time I…
  • …last Monday
  • …two days ago
  • …at the weekend
  • …last summer
  • It was…
Ask your partner: “When was the last time you…?”

Listen to the questions first. Then interview each other.

Stage 10 · Type it

Type it

Now produce it — type, don’t tap.

Spelling counts. Type the answers, then check.

1Last night I ___ a film. (watch)
2She ___ to work by bus yesterday. (go)
3We ___ dinner at eight. (have)
Why

Regular verbs + -ed (watched, finished, started) \u00b7 irregular change the word: go \u2192 went, have \u2192 had.

1I goed home early.
2She watch a film yesterday.
3We haved dinner at eight.
Why

Regular verbs + -ed (watched, finished, started) \u00b7 irregular change the word: go \u2192 went, have \u2192 had.

1Rewrite in the past: I finish work at six.
2Rewrite in the past: She goes to school.
3Rewrite in the past: We start at nine.
Why

Regular verbs + -ed (watched, finished, started) \u00b7 irregular change the word: go \u2192 went, have \u2192 had.
